title: Fetch the local ramp fixture
objective: Make a request and render its JSON response through the existing effect.
tasks: In loadRamps call fetch(url, { signal }), await the response, and return its parsed JSON as Ramp[].
Keep loadLocalRamps and /public/ramps.json unchanged; the adapter supports the preview and local Vite paths.
Confirm the preview moves from an empty result to the three named ramps.
hints: The temporary Ramp[] assertion describes the expected shape; the next lesson will validate it at runtime.

title: Reject HTTP and invalid data
objective: Validate the response before treating it as ramp data.
tasks: Check response.ok before JSON parsing; throw an Error containing response.status for a failed HTTP response.
Parse JSON as unknown and require an array of objects with string id and name fields before returning Ramp[].
Toggle the missing fixture to inspect the error UI, then restore the working URL.
Temporarily change a fixture name to a number to exercise invalid data; restore the file afterwards.
hints: fetch can resolve on 404: a resolved promise is not the same as an OK HTTP status.
A Vite missing path may return HTML with status 200; the JSON parse error must still reach the error UI.

title: Cancel obsolete requests
objective: Pair every effect request with cancellation and stale-result protection.
tasks: Create an AbortController inside each effect setup and pass controller.signal to loadLocalRamps.
In cleanup set active to false before calling controller.abort().
Keep both success and error handlers guarded by active; rapidly toggle the missing-fixture option and check the final selection wins.
hints: Create the controller inside useEffect so each request gets its own signal.
The active guard ignores stale completions; abort stops unnecessary work. Keep both.

title: Retry the same request
objective: Start a fresh request without changing the URL or reloading the page.
tasks: Add a request counter with useState(0).
Enable Retry request and increment that counter with a functional update on each click.
Include request in the effect dependencies alongside url; retry success and failure, then restore the working fixture.
hints: Changing a dependency reruns the effect even when url is unchanged.
The existing effect resets loading and error and cleans up the previous request; use that same path for retry.
